task_instance: Mode 1 (Design Review): review a small React 'AI Feedback Widget' component (sample-app/FeedbackWidget.jsx) against the skill's three quality pillars (Frictionless Insight-to-Action, Quality is Craft, Trustworthy Building), score/prioritize issues as blocking/major/minor, and produce a written review with recommendations, verifying at least one accessibility claim with an automated tool (axe-core) rather than assertion alone.
evidence: Created a representative sample component with intentional design/a11y/trust issues at sample-app/FeedbackWidget.jsx. Conducted the full review process from SKILL.md (identify task -> check design tokens -> evaluate aesthetic direction -> scope -> evaluate each pillar -> score/prioritize -> recommendations) and wrote the output to design-review.md, including a scored issue table (1 blocking, 4 major, 2 minor) and concrete fix recommendations. To avoid an unverified accessibility claim, installed axe-core + jsdom (npm install --no-save axe-core jsdom; succeeded, confirming outbound network/npm registry access works) and wrote verify_a11y.js, which renders static markup mirroring the component's before/after DOM and runs `axe.run()` against it. Ran `node verify_a11y.js`: axe-core reported 0 violations tied to the input's accessible name in both versions (placeholder counts as a valid accessible name per the HTML accname algorithm), which corrected an initial overstated 'blocking WCAG failure' claim down to a 'major best-practice/robustness' finding in the final review doc. Files: /tmp/.../microsoft__skills__frontend-design-review/sample-app/FeedbackWidget.jsx, /tmp/.../microsoft__skills__frontend-design-review/verify_a11y.js, /tmp/.../microsoft__skills__frontend-design-review/design-review.md (the deliverable). No Storybook/Figma integration was available or needed for this instance; those steps in the skill are optional workflow inputs, not required for producing a valid design review, and their absence was explicitly noted in the review rather than faked.
